title: EveryApp puts agent-built business tools inside your own Cloudflare account
summary: EveryApp puts agent-built business tools inside your own Cloudflare account
body_markdown:
Building a small business app with a coding agent is one task; giving a team a reliable place to use it is another.[EveryApp](https://everyapp.com/) is launching a self-hosted platform that runs open-source and custom applications behind a shared gateway in the customer's own Cloudflare account.


Founder Ben Senescu's ambition is broad: open-source alternatives to the software businesses routinely buy. The immediate release is more specific. It provides a common way to deploy those applications, manage access and connect them to agents, reducing the infrastructure decisions required for each new internal tool.


EveryApp says all requests pass through its Gateway and applications have no public address of their own. Authentication uses Cloudflare Access. For external integrations, an app requests access through the Gateway, which makes the call without handing the API key to the app.


Those are useful architectural boundaries to inspect, rather than a guarantee that any application built on the platform will be secure. They centralize decisions that otherwise tend to be repeated across internal tools: who may open an app, how it calls an external service and where credentials are kept.


Applications also become accessible through EveryApp's MCP Gateway. The intended result is a collection of tools that people and their agents can reach through a common interface, including software a company builds for itself.


[Watch EveryApp's launch demonstration](https://youtu.be/krDediTp0MI) .


The platform imposes a technical constraint along with that convenience. Applications must run on Cloudflare's primitives, including services such as KV and R2. EveryApp provides a preferred stack and component library, so a team starts with established conventions rather than defining a new deployment pattern for every project.


Senescu says an earlier version of EveryApp launched in January without enough useful applications to give people a reason to adopt the platform. He then built OpenSEO as a standalone product. In the new announcement, he reports more than 24,000 GitHub stars and thousands of customers for OpenSEO. Those are company-reported figures for that product, not a count of EveryApp platform customers.


The official site now lists OpenSEO alongside OpenCRM, OpenAnalytics and OpenMail, and points users to the[EveryApp repository](https://github.com/every-app/every-app) . The proposition is to run an existing application or fork it as the starting point for something specific to a business.


The current launch is the self-hosted edition. EveryApp says it plans to make money from a managed service starting at $10 a month and increasing with usage. Its announcement also cites Cloudflare's $5 monthly paid plan as a hosting starting point; actual costs will depend on the services and usage involved. The managed offering should not be confused with what is shipping in the self-hosted release.


Senescu previously worked as a senior software engineer at Klaviyo and as a founding engineer building compliance agents. EveryApp is part of Y Combinator's Fall 2026 batch.


The appeal rests on whether a standard deployment environment makes maintaining these applications manageable after the agent finishes writing them. Owning the code gives a team room to adapt a tool. EveryApp is trying to make that ownership come with a repeatable way to run it.
